clue.text: On the pavement, you'll see a snake! Stop!

parts.note: the asp is a small venomous snake, the one that killed Cleopatra
to halt is to stop, and Halt! is the command

explanation.surface: A walker spots a snake on the footpath and cries out to freeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the tarry surfacing laid on roads and paths, so it is the paving material itself.

clue.text: Everything was due to being permitted.

parts.note: all means everything
owed means was due, as a debt is

explanation.surface: Someone claims everything was owed to them because they had permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowed and permitted are synonyms: both mean given leave to do something.

clue.text: Adaptable, or maybe phony, as shown in blurry last pic.

indicators.note: a blurry photo has its details jumbled, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A judgement on a blurred final photograph that shows something fake or flexible.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic means mouldable or adaptable, and also artificial or fake, as in a plastic smile.

clue.text: What the determined partygoer looks for to destroy self-confidence.

wordplay.words: What the determined partygoer looks for
wordplay.note: a bash is a lively party, so a party animal goes looking for a bash

explanation.surface: A dedicated reveller's search somehow ends up crushing someone's confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash someone is to embarrass and disconcert them, making them lose their poise.

clue.text: Come down heavily with your feet, and in Paris getting up in it to be given something nice.

indicators.note: the French word goes into it, the tread just mentioned

parts.words: Come down heavily with your feet
parts.note: to tread is to step down firmly

indicators.note: in a down answer, getting up means the word is written from the bottom upward

parts.note: et is the French for and

explanation.surface: Stamping on something in Paris somehow leads to a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: To be treated is to be given a treat, a gift or outing laid on as a kindness.

clue.text: How hot air might come to you–or something that runs over the valley.

definitions.text: something that runs over the valley

parts.note: via means by way of, answering the question how something gets somewhere

parts.words: hot air might come to you
parts.note: in a heating system warm air reaches a room through a duct

explanation.surface: Musing on central heating, then on a bridge spanning a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a phrase split into two words: hot air comes 'via duct'.
explanation.definitionFit: A viaduct is a long bridge carrying a road or railway across a valley on a row of arches.

clue.text: Ships containers.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: pots, jugs and other holders

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ships' looks like a verb (it ships containers), but it is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both seagoing craft and receptacles such as bowls and jars.

clue.text: A lousy performance, but a deadly thing to drop.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... is a flop, a show that fails badly
second meaning: an atomic bomb, dropped from a plane

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the answer as the article plus the slang for a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as one word it is the atomic bomb; read as two it is a theatrical failure.

clue.text: A complete description to the news boss, in short, it is said.

parts.note: utter means complete, absolute, as in utter nonsense
Ed is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone gives the newspaper's editor a full report, so it is claimed.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter words is to speak them, so uttered means spoken aloud or said.

clue.text: An old photo shows what the steno might do following the money in London.

indicators.note: tells us the typing comes after the money

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money
a stenographer types up dictation

explanation.surface: An old photograph shows a London typist at work beside some cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A tintype is a 19th-century photograph printed directly onto a thin sheet of iron.

clue.text: You don't want to have things come out this way–you'll see it in certain people–aka Generals.

definitions.text: You don't want to have things come out this way

indicators.note: says the answer is sitting inside the following run of words, spanning their joins

parts.note: the words that hold the answer, read straight through ignoring the dash and spaces

explanation.surface: A grumble about secrets escaping through certain people, namely the generals.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of 'people', all of 'aka' and the start of 'Generals'.
explanation.definitionFit: A leakage is an unwanted escape of fluid or information, the way you would not want things to get out.

clue.text: Cut a bit off to do it, and in Paris it returns in a clipped fashion.

parts.note: short means brief or clipped, as in a short reply
en is the French pronoun meaning 'of it', so it is what 'it' becomes in Paris

explanation.surface: Advice on trimming something, with a French aside about a clipped manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' only carries the surface: the French word simply comes after the English one.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten something is to reduce its length by removing a piece of it.

clue.text: Good employees shouldn't do it to clock what might be a small version of the clock.

definitions.text: Good employees shouldn't do it to clock
definitions.meaning: first meaning: to clock-... is to keep looking at the time waiting for work to end

definitions.text: what might be a small version of the clock
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a timepiece worn on the wrist or carried in a pocket

explanation.surface: Office etiquette about staring at the clock, then a remark about miniature clocks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for keeping an eye on the time and the noun for a portable timepiece.

clue.text: One of the lowest digits, if you get to a point here.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a digit of the foot, the lowest on the body

definitions.text: if you get to a point here
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a ballet dancer rising on pointe stands on the tips of the feet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Digits' looks numerical, as if 'lowest' meant 0 or 1, but these are the digits on your feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Toes are the digits at the bottom of the body, and dancers balance on their tips when on point.

clue.text: By the sound of it to inter a straw type, or a rasp type.

definitions.text: a straw type, or a rasp type

indicators.note: tells us to swap the word for one that is pronounced the same

parts.note: to inter a body is to bury it

explanation.surface: A puzzling note on burying straw, or perhaps a rasp, a coarse file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straw' and 'rasp' are clipped: put the answer after each to get strawberry and raspberry.
explanation.definitionFit: The strawberry and the raspberry are both kinds of soft fruit, each named with this ending.

clue.text: The answer might be rotten, but you'll find it a small island indeed!

indicators.note: says the island is found within the following word

parts.note: a deed is an act, the word hidden in plain sight as in-deed
a cay is a small low island or reef, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.surface: Someone warns that the reply may be poor but promises a tiny island.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the phrase 'the answer might be rotten': the answer means rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Decayed food or wood has gone bad and broken down, which is what rotten describes.

clue.text: See 27 across
In a cross-wind, less likely to be what you don't want someone to do to you.

definitions.text: what you don't want someone to do to you

indicators.note: the answer is held inside the words that follow, running across the hyphen and comma

parts.note: the words that hold the answer, read straight through ignoring the hyphen and comma

explanation.surface: Sailing talk: a crosswind is less likely to do something unwelcome to you.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer starts with the last letter of 'cross' and ends inside 'less'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cheated or conned out of money is something nobody wants done to them.

clue.text: See 26 across
If you hear 11 with the birdie, someone may be getting ready to shoot you to make it!

definitions.text: If you hear 11 with the birdie, someone may be getting ready to shoot you to make it!

parts.words: If you hear 11 with the birdie
parts.note: 11 is the across answer meaning look at; 'watch the birdie' is the photographer's old call to make a sitter look at the camera

parts.words: someone may be getting ready to shoot you to make it
parts.note: the shooting is with a camera, not a gun, and the result is a photograph

explanation.surface: A sinister warning that someone may be about to shoot you.
explanation.walkthrough: The menace is a pun: to shoot here is to photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is the photograph a camera operator takes after telling the sitter to look at the lens.

clue.text: Getting quiet, lifts up encomiums.

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, meaning quiet
raises means lifts up

explanation.surface: As the room quietens, the tributes are raised aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: Encomiums are formal speeches or writings of high praise, so the plural praises fits.

clue.text: An exclusive group with the lake bed turned over.

indicators.note: the two words are read in the opposite order to the clue's

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A select club and a lakebed somehow turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lake bed' looks like one thing, the floor of a lake; it is two pieces whose order is swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small, select circle of people with shared interests who keep others out.

clue.text: Do 7 without the boss, as part of the noun, certainly.

definitions.note: 7 is the down answer meaning said; take off its Ed, the editor, and 'do utter' means speak

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the words that follow, running across their joins

parts.note: the words that hold the answer, read straight through ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: A grammar instruction about a word without its head, part of a noun.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition needs a step: remove the editor from 7's answer to get utter, and to do that is to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: To enounce is to pronounce or state something, which is what uttering words means.

clue.text: How could a mess of gruel be so responsible for one of the above?

definitions.text: responsible for one of the above

indicators.note: a mess of something is a jumble, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: thin porridge, here just supplying its letters
taken as written, its letters joining the jumble

explanation.surface: Wondering how a mess of porridge could be to blame for something mentioned earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of the above' points to the answer just above this one, which is a painting; the Flemish painter Breugel made many.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is the person who creates a picture, so the Flemish master is responsible for one.

clue.text: With one's hands, bangs the sideboards.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to buffet is to strike repeatedly, as with blows of the hand
second meaning: a buffet is a piece of dining-room furniture for serving food

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bangs' looks like a noun (a fringe of hair), but it is the verb to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for repeated blows and the plural of a serving cabinet.

clue.text: Commonly deteriorate what the gardener might do to plant things.

definitions.text: what the gardener might do to plant things
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a gardener goes to a flowerpot to plant seedlings

explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' marks the first sense as an informal idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go to ruin; taken literally, a gardener heads to a pot to plant in it.

clue.text: With a great letter you get the word for lavish giving.

indicators.note: spoken together, the two pieces sound like the term that follows, so the clue works by ear

parts.note: a great big letter S is a large S

explanation.surface: A grand letter turns out to spell a word for generous gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'large S' and you hear the answer; the spelling doubles the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess, or largesse, is generosity in handing out money or gifts freely.

clue.text: A relatively high spot characteristic of Greece?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the room at the top of a house, under the roof
second meaning: of Attica, the region of Athens, and so Greek in style

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second sense as a stretch: strictly, Attic is Athenian rather than all Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the top floor under the eaves; the adjective describes things from ancient Athens.

clue.text: Improperly teach a swindling type.

indicators.note: something done improperly is done wrongly, so the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written, its letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: Teaching badly is the mark of a con artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat is a person who swindles or deceives others for gain.

clue.text: Where many a person works away from the frozen surface.

parts.note: off means away from, as in off the road
ice is the frozen surface of a pond or rink

explanation.surface: Office workers are pictured as people who stay well clear of the ice rink.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is split over two lights: the across part and the down part joined to it.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is the workplace of a great many clerical and professional staff.

clue.text: A polite expression at the revolving door.

definitions.text: A polite expression at the revolving door.

parts.note: a courteous phrase of the sort said when letting someone else go first
a doorway that only lets one person through at a time, so someone must defer

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is split over two lights: the across part and the down part joined to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The courteous phrase offers someone else the turn to go first, as when two people meet at a single doorway.

clue.text: A pull-up as a prize.

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to draw is to pull, as a horse draws a cart

explanation.surface: A pull-up at the gym is offered as a reward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull-up' looks like the gym exercise; it is 'pull' plus a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize given for achievement.

clue.text: The specialist medico is evidently told to go ahead with a rush!

parts.note: to surge is to move forward suddenly in a rush
on is the word for going forward, as in 'carry on'

explanation.surface: A specialist doctor is apparently being urged to hurry forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is evidently told to' is the setter's way of saying the doctor's title, split, is an order: 'surge on!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a doctor who specialises in operations rather than general practice.

clue.text: One's former mate has plenty, for instance!

parts.note: an ex is a former husband, wife or partner
ample means more than enough, plentiful

explanation.surface: Someone's ex-partner is said to have lots, offered as an instance of something.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a case given for instance, a specimen illustrating a general point.

clue.text: She gets the sort of heat you can use to carry your arm in.

definitions.text: use to carry your arm in

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a sort of heat means a version of the word, its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, its letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: A woman gets a kind of warmth, apparently useful for carrying a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' is a weapon here, not a limb: a sword is carried in its scabbard.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe a blade is to put it in its scabbard, the case a sword or knife is carried in.

clue.text: Eased a test situation, to show how one calms down.

indicators.note: the situation, or position, of the answer is inside the preceding words, across their joins

parts.note: the words that hold the answer, read straight through ignoring spaces

explanation.surface: An examiner relaxed the conditions of a test, which shows how someone settles down.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer starts in 'Eased', runs through 'a' and ends in 'test'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sedate someone is to make them calm, often with a drug, so it means calms down.
